To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

serum potassium monitoring should be carried out at least monthly in the following risk groups: patients receiving YK preparations, co-administration of lower potassium-inducing drug (LPID) such as diuretics, mineralocorticoid or glucocorticoid, hypoalbuminaemic state and patients receiving a full dosage of YK preparations.

the risk factors for hypokaemia in patients treated YK preparations are: co-administration of lower potassium-inducing diuretics and glucocorticoids; YK preparation administration (not YCH); hypoalbuminaemia and full dosage administration.

the risk factors for hypocalcaemia in patients treated by Yokukansan, which is a traditional Kampo medicine in Japan.

the risk of hypokalemia is increased in patients treated with YOKUKANSAN preparations who are also receiving other medications that can lower serum potassium levels, such as diuretics and glucocorticoids.
the risk of hypokalaemic events in patients taking YK preparations is not negligible, and should be monitored carefully.

the risk factors of liquorice-induced hypokalemia are as follows: 1) co-administration of lower potassium-inducing drug (such as diuretics, glycyrrhiza, glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid); 2) administration of Yokukansan; 3) hypoalbuminaemia; and 4) full dosage administration (more than 7.5 g/day).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found the risk factors for hypocalcaemia induced by Kampo medicine in the patients with dementia and other psychiatric diseases, which are the coadministration of the drugs inducing hypocalcaemia, the administration of the Kampo medicine, and the hypoalbuminemia.
we have identified the risk factors for hypkalaemia induced by YK preparations, which would be useful for the prevention of hypokalaemic events in the patients treated with YKP preparations.

the risk factors of YK preparation-induced potassium depletion are: 1) YK administration (but not YKCH), 2) co-administration with LPIDs, 3) hypoalbuminaemia (but not low serum potassium levels) at baseline, and 4) full dosage administration (≥7.5 mg/day).
The main takeaway from our work is that
serum potassium levels should be monitored monthly in patients with dementia who are treated with YK or YKCH preparations.
the incidence of hypokalaemic events was significantly higher in patients who received Yokukansan than in those who received Yokukan-san-ka-chin-pi-hange.
the risk factors for hypokaemia induced by liquorice preparations are: 1) the type of preparation, 2) co-administration of drugs that lower potassium levels, 3) low albumin level and 4) high dose.
